sections.html:
The option period is a window in which a buyer who paid an agreed option fee can end the contract for any reason by giving the seller written notice. The termination option is a negotiable term, so a buyer does not have to pay for one.

Buyers typically use the days to inspect the house and negotiate repairs through an amendment, or to walk away. For a seller, the period is the stretch in which the deal can end without the buyer giving a reason, so the numbers written into the contract matter.

Resale of a single family home, duplex, triplex or fourplex uses the One to Four Family Residential Contract (Resale), Form 20-19, with an effective date of July 1, 2026. It is the most frequently used contract form.

It is not for condominium sales, new homes sold by a builder, or farm and ranch property, and TREC publishes separate forms for those. TREC's contracts page also offers many addenda, including a third party financing addendum, a seller financing addendum, a short sale addendum and a back-up contract addendum.

The buyer delivers earnest money and the option fee to the escrow agent. An earlier edition of the form, in paragraph 5A, required delivery within three days of the effective date. Paragraph 5D set the consequence: if no option fee amount is stated or the buyer fails to deliver it on time, the buyer has no unrestricted right to terminate under that paragraph.

Paragraph numbers and day counts can shift between editions, so read the current 20-19 itself or ask your agent or title company to point them out. Days count from the effective date, with the first day being the next day, and each day is a calendar day.

  • Option fee: set by the parties, paid to the seller for the termination right.
  • Earnest money: held by the escrow agent.
  • Option days: a negotiated number written into the contract.
  • Notice: written, delivered to the other side.

The count starts with the effective date, which is the date of final signature, and the first day of any period is the day after. Every day is a calendar day, so weekends and holidays count. If you sign on a Friday, Saturday is day one. Ask your agent to mark the end date on a calendar.

Send deadline notices the way the contract's notice paragraph requires, because a missed deadline can change what a party may do. TREC does not decide whether a contract is valid or which party wins a dispute, so keep a dated copy of every notice sent or received.

sections.h2: When the buyer never pays earnest money
sections.html:
TREC's forms require the buyer to deliver earnest money to the escrow agent. If the buyer does not deliver it on time, the seller may terminate or exercise remedies under the contract's default paragraph. TREC has no jurisdiction to decide who is entitled to earnest money.

If a dispute over earnest money arises, talk to a private attorney. TREC has no authority over title companies, though it can take complaints about a license holder who fails to deposit earnest money as the contract requires.

sections.h2: What a Texas seller must disclose
sections.html:
Sellers of previously occupied single family homes complete the Seller's Disclosure Notice, TREC Form 55-1, effective May 28, 2026. The form covers information required by Section 5.008 of the Property Code about material facts and the physical condition of the property, and applies with a contract entered into on or after September 1, 2023.

Give the notice completely and accurately, and ask your agent how to answer any question about repairs or known defects. A mistake in completing a form can lead to financial loss or an unenforceable contract.

sections.h2: How repair terms and the option period fit together
sections.html:
A buyer should check the box for specific repairs only if particular repairs are known when the contract is signed. Otherwise the buyer checks the as-is box, and most buyers then pay for an option period to inspect and negotiate.

Repair paths in the resale contract
SituationWhat to do
Specific repairs known at signingUse the specific-repairs choice and list them
No known repairsUse the as-is choice
Repairs found by inspectionAmend the contract, or terminate during the option period
Boxes left blank or vagueNot permitted

As a seller, expect repair requests to come through an amendment after the buyer inspects. The option period is when that bargaining happens.

sections.h2: Can I use a TREC form without an agent?
sections.html:
Yes. The contract forms are available for public use, but they are intended primarily for brokers and sales agents trained in using them. A mistake in using a form may lead to financial loss or an unenforceable contract, and a person using a form accepts all risks that come with it.

A license holder who fills in a form may add only factual matters and business details to a form adopted for mandatory use. If TREC has not promulgated a form that you need, have an attorney draft it. A license holder may not draft an instrument that transfers or affects an interest in real property.

  • A Texas real estate attorney can draft terms the forms do not cover.
  • Members of the Texas Association of Realtors can use that group's forms.
  • Your title company can explain how it handles earnest money and the option fee.

sections.h2: What to check in the contract before you sign
sections.html:
Find the option days, the option fee, the earnest money amount and the repair choice. These are blanks or checkboxes that the parties fill in, and complete and accurate completion is the license holder's duty.

  • The effective date is filled in.
  • The option fee amount is stated, and a due date for delivery.
  • The earnest money amount and the escrow agent are named.
  • The repair paragraph has one choice marked, not both and not neither.
  • Any addendum, such as financing or a back-up contract, is attached.

Whether a contract with a blank effective date is valid is a question for a private attorney, so catch blanks before signing.

A buyer who wants to terminate can use TREC's Notice of Buyer's Termination of Contract form, and a seller has a matching Notice of Seller's Termination form. Notices need to reach the other side in the way the contract requires, so check the notice paragraph in your form.

License holders must use adopted contract forms and may add only factual matters and business details. No TREC form is meant to be a contract for deed. Anyone who needs something the forms do not cover should have an attorney prepare it. A blank effective date or a disputed term goes to a private attorney.

A seller weighing a cash buyer should know that option periods, financing addenda and repair amendments are all negotiable, and a cash offer often shortens or drops several of them. Read whatever terms a buyer proposes the same way you would read any other contract.

faqs.q: Is an option period required in a Texas home contract?
faqs.a: No. The termination option is a negotiable term and a buyer does not have to pay for one. A buyer who pays the agreed fee gets the right to terminate for any reason by written notice during the option period.

faqs.q: How long is the option period?
faqs.a: The parties negotiate it, and the number of days is written into the contract. Check the figure in your signed form.

faqs.q: What if the buyer did not pay the option fee?
faqs.a: Probably no unrestricted termination right. A buyer who states no fee or fails to deliver it on time loses that right under the option paragraph.

faqs.q: Which form applies to my Texas house sale?
faqs.a: Form 20-19, effective July 1, 2026, for single family homes and two to four unit residential properties. TREC lists separate forms for condos, new builds and farm and ranch property.

faqs.q: Can TREC decide an earnest money dispute?
faqs.a: No. TREC lacks jurisdiction over who is entitled to earnest money and refers parties to a private attorney.
